The test image shows a tomato leaf with prominent dark, concentric ring-like necrotic lesions covering much of the leaf surface. The rings are circular/oval, dark brown to black, with green centers — a classic "ring spot" pattern. This strongly suggests Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (TSWV), which is well known for this exact symptom.

Now I'll view one reference image from that class to confirm.

The reference image shows an early-stage TSWV presentation (small scattered specks, bronzing). The test image shows a more advanced TSWV presentation — the large, dark concentric ring spots are the hallmark symptom of this virus. TSWV is well documented to cause exactly these ring-within-ring necrotic patterns on tomato leaves as the infection progresses. The pattern in the test image doesn't match Early Blight (which has discrete bullseye spots with yellow halos) or any fungal disease.
